title: Related party transactions
subject: This guide provides guidance on promoting better disclosure and governance for related party transactions under the Corporations Act. It covers the legal framework, directors' voting restrictions, financial reporting requirements, and ASIC's approach to granting relief.
background: The guide is issued under ASIC's administration of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), particularly Chapter 2E which regulates related party transactions to protect members' interests. It is intended for public companies, responsible entities of registered managed investment schemes, experts, public company directors, and their professional advisers.
ruling: ASIC expects entities to fully disclose related party transactions in financial reports and to comply with the member approval requirements under Chapter 2E. ASIC will consider granting relief from these requirements in limited circumstances, such as where the transaction is on arm's length terms or where strict compliance would cause undue hardship. The guide outlines ASIC's approach to assessing applications for relief, including the need for independent expert reports and shareholder approval. ASIC also provides guidance on directors' voting restrictions under section 195 when they have a material personal interest. ASIC emphasizes that the overarching principle is to ensure transparency and protect the interests of members.
